resources.string: The terminal tab is the main workspace: Linux terminal, shortcut rows, and the command wheel.
Shortcut rows and Ctrl mode

Adds the control keys a screen keyboard lacks.
▸ `/` `Tab` `Esc` `Ctrl` on the top row — tap to send
▸ Tap `Ctrl` — arm it (the button turns red); the next key is sent with Ctrl
▸ Tap an arrow — move the cursor; while armed, arrows jump word by word
▸ The Back key — sends Esc (terminal tab only)
⚠ Arming auto-resets after 3 seconds without input.
Showing and hiding the keyboard
▸ Double-tap the terminal — hides the keyboard if shown, shows it if hidden
Command wheel

A visual wheel for frequent commands: swipe to pick, tap to run.
▸ Swipe up / down on the shortcut bar — switch between shortcut rows and the command wheel
▸ Swipe horizontally — the centered card is highlighted; tap it to run
▸ A centered group — expands its members automatically
▸ Tap the gray area — collapse the wheel; long-press it — open the command library
● Recommendations rank by frequency, order and recency, so likely commands land in the center.
Command library

Sort, group, back up and restore commands (long-press the gray area in the wheel to enter).
▸ Long-press and drag — reorder
▸ Tap a command or group — open it for editing
▸ Swipe a command left — delete; swipe a group left — dissolve; members can be moved out or deleted by swiping
● Each group keeps at least 2 members.
● Backup and restore are supported; restored commands rejoin ranking.
● Syntax: supports `\n \r \t \e \cX`; `@{}` marks where the cursor lands after running.
Startup and tile commands

When the two preset commands run (fill them in on the Settings tab).\n● Startup command — runs automatically when the terminal starts\n● Tile command — runs when launched from the tile; fits one-tap preset actions
termlou-ui script dialogs

One shell line opens a native dialog.
● Forms: input | single choice | multiple choice | toggle | colored text output
● Styles: theme, accent, corners, position, animation, auto-close timeout
● `termlou-clipboard` — writes text straight to the system clipboard
Dialog and splash workshops
Two visual design tools.\n● Dialog workshop — design dialogs visually, live preview, export termlou-ui commands\n● Splash workshop — draw pixel art, convert photos to pixels, particle boot animation

Notes are fully local: the list manages notes and the editor holds text, tags and todos; the two buttons at the bottom open the Todos and Calendar views, and focusing the search box floats up the tag filter row.
List and editor

The note directory and editor.
● Each list row: title | updated time | tag capsules
▸ The + button at the bottom right — create a note
▸ Tap a note — open the editor (title, body, tags and todos in separate zones)
▸ Long-press a note — rename
▸ The Todos and Calendar buttons at the bottom — open the matching views
Search

One search box sits on top of the note list and the Todos view (the Calendar view has none), all sharing the same rules.
● All fields — title, tags, body and its todos are searched together
● Multi-word — split by spaces; all terms must match; terms can span fields
● Typos — homophone tolerance: a homophone typo still finds the word
● Pinyin — full pinyin `pingguo`, initials `pg`, or homophones
▸ Focus the search box — a translucent tag filter row floats up from the bottom; scroll it sideways and tap tags to filter
▸ Tag capsules enter the search box — selecting one filters by the `tag:name` field; tap the capsule again to remove it; multiple tags are ANDed
▸ The Back key — clears the search text and tag capsules first, then leaves the page
● Results appear 200 ms after you stop typing; 10,000 notes still answer in milliseconds.
Tag filtering

Colored capsules that group your notes.
● Color comes from a content hash — the same tag always has the same color
▸ Focus the search box — the bottom filter row lists every tag; tap to toggle
▸ A selected tag — becomes a `#tag ×` capsule in the search box and only keeps notes carrying it; multiple tags are ANDed
▸ Tap a capsule inside the search box — remove that tag filter
▸ In the editor, the + Tags button adds one; tapping a capsule removes it
Todos view

A two-column board for global todos (enter from the Todos button at the bottom of the list).
● Left = done, right = open; each column scrolls on its own with a frozen title
▸ Tap a row — toggle done / open
▸ Long-press a row — delete
● Changes are saved immediately.
Calendar view

A month calendar for notes and todos (enter from the Calendar button at the bottom of the list).
● Weeks start on Monday and the last week pads only to Sunday — never an extra row; the whole block of cells is vertically centered and each cell is nearly square
● A filled cell = a note exists that day; transparent = none (notes no longer get an icon)
● Small in-cell icons: todo state (red = all open, yellow = partially done, green = all done; hidden when the day has no todos) + a gray price tag = the day has tags
▸ Swipe up / down — previous / next month, and it works anywhere on the page
▸ At the oldest month with content — blocked with No older notes yet; into the future — blocked with The future has not arrived yet
▸ Tap the month title (2026 Sep) — jump back to the current month
▸ Tap a day — day details: all tags, the todo status, and that day notes in one index
▸ Tap a note in the index — open the editor right away, no step in between
⚠ The gray out-of-month dates padded in are not tappable.
Auto save

Leaving the editor saves; there is nothing to press.
▸ Leaving the editor — writes only when the body changed
● Triggers: leave the list | switch note | switch tab | go to background | open a subpage
● Typing never touches the disk, so there is no per-keystroke write amplification.
Tile shortcut

Jump straight to notes from the home-screen tile.
▸ The tile — opens the standalone notes page directly
● Never wakes the terminal or the Linux session
● Exiting returns to the launcher; nothing stays in the background.
The files tab manages `/workspace`: navigation, import, sharing, and deletion.
Navigation and info

Browse the `/workspace` tree.
▸ Tap a folder — enter it (the list fades in)
▸ The back FAB at bottom right — go up one level; at the root the arrow dims and a tap says there is no parent folder
● Folders are highlighted; file rows show their size (B / KB / MB)
● After entering a folder, the status line briefly shows the current path.
Import

Bring outside content into the current folder.
▸ The Import file button at the bottom — any format, multiple selection supported
▸ The Import folder button at the bottom — imports a whole folder recursively
● Import target = the folder you have open.
Share and export
Send files out.\n▸ Tap a file or long-press a folder — open the Export and Delete menu\n▸ Choose Export — files go to the system share sheet; folders are packed as ZIP first
Delete

Remove items from the current folder.
▸ Tap a file or long-press a folder — pick Delete in the menu
▸ Files — deleted directly; non-empty folders — confirm first
⚠ Deletion is immediate; there is no recycle bin.
Type recognition
Recognized by file extension.\n● Automatically told apart: text | images | archives | code | documents
Settings holds all switches and commands; language needs a restart, the palette applies instantly.
Display

Everything display-related lives here.
● Terminal font size — five steps, applied instantly
● Language — Chinese / English
● Color palette — custom background + theme green, other colors derived from the background; saved instantly, one tap to restore defaults
⚠ Language needs an app restart; font size and palette apply immediately.
Notes

Everything notes-related lives here.
● Auto-delete empty notes — when on, a note with no text and no todos is deleted without asking (tags are not content)
● When it fires — when leaving the editor, or deleting the last todo on the board
● Default off — when off, a dialog asks whether to delete
Commands

Where the preset commands are filled in (see the terminal tab).
● Startup command — runs when the terminal starts
● Tile command — runs when launched from the tile
● Quick launch — pick favorite apps for one-tap opening
Workshops
Entries to the two workshops (see the terminal tab).\n● Dialog workshop — design script dialogs and export commands\n● Splash workshop — draw freely or import an image for the boot screen
Sharing, browser and keep-alive

LAN sharing, the built-in browser and background residency.
● LAN share — share files and the terminal over the local network
● Browser — drives web pages for the Linux-side AI agent; generic mobile UA, cookies persist for login
● Keep-alive — a low-priority foreground service keeps the app alive
